text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > build/memory/pr-body.md <<'MD'
Analysis of a medium-sized project could exhaust 4 GiB at `CacheCodec.php:22` while allocating another copy of the serialized graph. Cache reads also copied entire entries and retained stale payloads during recomputation, while native analysis and call enrichment retained project-wide syntax trees.

This change streams checksum-protected graph batches to atomic cache files and rebuilds inverse edges and lookup indexes during reads. It validates the input fingerprint before reading a payload. Native analysis now indexes declaration locations and loads syntax on demand; call enrichment releases processed expression trees. The source walker no longer forms a retention cycle or materializes persistent property tables, repeated declarations are deduplicated early, and authored edges retain endpoint IDs instead of endpoint objects.

A generated 300,000-line corpus (3,000 files, 9,000 nodes, 267,000 forward edges) on PHP 8.5.8 with Xdebug disabled produced these PHP peak allocation measurements:

| Operation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold analysis and cache write | 3,998 MiB | 920 MiB |
| Completed graph cache hit | — | 1,724 MiB |
| Rebuild with existing cache entries | Exhausted 4 GiB at `CacheCodec.php:22` | 920 MiB |

All three updated paths complete with `memory_limit=2G`. These are synthetic measurements; graph size and source structure still determine memory requirements. Reading files on demand trades some repeated parsing for bounded syntax retention.

Regression coverage includes cold, warm, edited and re-warmed analysis in separate 256 MiB processes; lifecycle checks using weak references; damaged, truncated and missing cache batches; atomic write cleanup; and cached call arguments, closures and possible dispatches with both engines.

Validation results will be filled in after the final checks finish.
MD
